questions.question: In which of the following states are the Sundargarh deposits of Manganese located ?

questions.question: Which district of Madhya Pradesh is a leading producer of copper?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Balaghat

Key Points

  • Balaghat:-
    • The Balaghat district of Madhya Pradesh is the leading producer of copper in the state.
    • It is home to the Malanjkhand Copper Project, which is the largest copper mine in India.
    • The Malanjkhand mine accounts for nearly 70% of the country's copper reserves and contributes around 80% to Hindustan Copper Limited's (HCL) total copper production.
    • In addition to the Malanjkhand mine, there are several other copper mines in the Balaghat district, including the Shitalpani, Gidhri Dhorli, Jatta, and Garhi Dongri mines.
    • The Balaghat district accounts for over 40% of India's total copper production.

Additional Information

  • Jabalpur district:-
    • It has several copper mines, including the Bagalkot, Rajarampahar, and Sonakhan mines.
    • These mines are operated by Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL). The Jabalpur district accounts for around 10% of Madhya Pradesh's total copper production.
  • Bhopal district:-
    • It has a few copper mines, including the Baijnath and Narsinghgarh mines.
    • These mines are also operated by HCL.
    • The Bhopal district accounts for around 5% of Madhya Pradesh's total copper production
  • Gwalior district:-
    • It has a few copper mines, including the Khaniyadhana and Morar mines.
    • These mines are operated by private companies.
    • The Gwalior district accounts for around 2% of Madhya Pradesh's total copper production.

questions.question: Quartz consists of ______.
questions.questionHtml: Quartz consists of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is silicon.

Key Points

  • Quartz is a mineral composed of silicon and oxygen, with a chemical composition of SiO2.
  • Metamorphic rocks contain abundant quartz especially those products from granites, sandstones, or shales.
  • Sandstones are pure quartz.
  • Rock crystal quartz is found widely distributed in the Alps, Brazil, Madagascar, and Japan.
  • Quartz exists in two forms, the normal temperature α-quartz, and the high-temperature β-quartz.
  • The hardness of the quartz is measured by Moh's Scale.

Additional Information

  • Quartz is one of the most useful natural materials. Its usefulness can be linked to its physical and chemical properties.
  • It is chemically inert in contact with most substances. It has electrical properties and heat resistance.
  • Its luster, color, and diaphaneity make it useful as a gemstone and also in the making of glass.
  • Use of quartz as an Abrasive: Quartz sands and finely ground silica sand are used for sand blasting, scouring cleansers, and grit for sanding and sawing.
  • Use of quartz in the Petrol industry.

questions.question: Which is the most popular coal in commercial use?
questions.questionHtml: Which is the most popular coal in commercial use?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bituminous.

Key Points:

  • Bituminous coal is a commercially used type of coal. 
  • Bituminous coal, also known as black coal, is a relatively soft coal that contains bitumen, a tar-like substance.
  • This coal is classified according to its plasticity, moisture content, volatility, and ash content.
  • Plasticity is required for the production of coke, which is used in the production of fuel gases such as producer gas.
  • Volatility is critical for steel production and power generation. 

Additional Information:

  • Anthracite:
    • ​Anthracite, also known as a hard coal, and a black coal, is hard, compact variety of coal that has a submetallic lustre.
    • It has the highest carbon content, the fewest impurities, and the highest energy density of any type of coal and is ranked first.
  • Peat:
    • Peat, also known as turf, is a type of organic matter that has partially decayed.
    • Turf differs from peat in that it also refers to soil with grass.
    • It can only be found in peatlands, bogs, mires, moors, or muskegs.
  • Lignite:
    • ​Lignite, also known as brown coal, is a soft, brown, combustible sedimentary rock composed of naturally compressed peat.

questions.question: Tummalapalle, believed to have one of the largest uranium reserves in the world, is situated in which of the following states?
questions.questionHtml: Tummalapalle, believed to have one of the largest uranium reserves in the world, is situated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

Important Points

  • The Tummalapalle Mine is a uranium mine located in Kadapa in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, in the village of Tumalapalli.
  • Results from research conducted by India's Atomic Energy Commission in 2011 have led analysts to conclude that this mine may have one of the world's largest uranium reserves. 
  • On 19 July 2011, Dr. S. Banerjee, Secretary of the Department of Atomic Energy, who was also Chairman of the Indian Atomic Energy Commission, confirmed reserves of 49,000 tonnes and suggested that it could be three times larger to make Tummalapalle the largest uranium deposit mine in the world.
  • In 2014, the estimates were subsequently raised to 85,000 tonnes.
  • Recent findings allegedly show that the reserves are as deep as 1,000 meters.
  • This finding has significantly increased India's ability to generate energy from nuclear power plants.
  • India produced about 3.13 percent of its energy from nuclear plants as of 2018.
  • These results indicate that this output can be increased to more than 30 percent by 2050, which is essential if India hopes to reduce its carbon emissions, pollution, and use.
  • Not only will this domestic uranium discovery improve India's nuclear energy ambitions, but it will also help cut costs by moving from costly electricity sources like coal.

Additional Information

    • Legislative Capital: Amaravati
    • Population: 4.94 crores (2011)
    • Chief minister: N. Chandrababu Naidu

questions.question: Which of the following minerals' primary constituent is iron oxide containing equal amounts of iron (II) and iron (III) that is mainly used for steel manufacturing?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following minerals' primary constituent is iron oxide containing equal amounts of iron (II) and iron (III) that is mainly used for steel manufacturing?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Magnetite.

  • Magnetite is a mineral whose primary component is an iron oxide that contains equal amounts of iron(II) and iron(III). Its empirical formula is Fe3O4, and it is often expressed as iron(II, III) oxide.

Key Points

  • Magnetite is found in igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary rocks.
  • As its name implies, it is magnetic; it and other inherently magnetic iron-containing minerals are described as being ferrimagnetic.
  • Magnetite is in the hexoctahedral crystal class; in the 3-D crystal structure, the purple atoms are iron, and the red atoms are oxygen.
  • Magnetite's greatest use is as important as iron ore for steel manufacture.
  • Other applications are as a catalyst in the Haber process for making ammonia, as a pigment for paints and ceramics, and as magnetic micro- and nanoparticles for a variety of processes and materials.

Additional Information

  • Iron oxides are among the most common minerals formed during rock weathering.
    • They vary in mineral species (goethite, hematite, lepidocrocite, maghemite, ferrihydrite) and, additionally for any mineral, in crystallinity and Al- for Fe-substitution in the structure.
  • Ferrous oxide, commonly known as iron(II) oxide contains iron that lost 2 electrons in the oxidation process. So it is able to bond with other atoms that have an extra 2 electrons. Ferric oxide, is commonly known as iron(III) oxide. It contains iron that lost 3 electrons.

questions.question: In India, tertiary coals occur in Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and ______.

The correct answer is Meghalaya.

Key Points

  • In India, tertiary coals occur in Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, and Meghalaya.
    • Tertiary coal is found in the rocks of the Oligocene period of the Tertiary Era.
    • Tertiary coal fields share only 1% of the coal production of India.
    • Tertiary coal is also known as 'brown coal'.
    • Tertiary coal contributes only about two per cent of the total coal production of the country. 
  • Hence, option 2 is correct. 

Additional Information

  • Coal is a combustible black or brownish-black sedimentary rock, formed as rock strata called coal seams.
    • Coal is the foremost power resources in India and is the most abundantly available fossil fuel.
    • India is highly dependent on coal for meeting its commercial energy requirements. 
    • Coal is found in a variety of forms depending on the degrees of compression and the depth and time of burial.
    • Types of Coal :
      •  Anthracite (more than 80% carbon content):
        •  In India, it is found only in Jammu and Kashmir.
      •  Bituminous (60 to 80 % Carbon Content):
        • It is the second-best quality of coal.
        • It is the most popular coal in commercial use.
      •  Peat (less than 40% carbon content)
      •  Lignite :
        •  It is low-grade brown coal, which is soft with high moisture content.
      • The principal lignite reserves are in Neyveli in Tamil Nadu and are used for the generation of electricity.
  • The Damodar Valley Coalfield is the largest coalfield in India that extended to Jharkhand and West Bengal.

questions.solution: Tertiary coals in India are primarily found in the northeastern states, with Meghalaya being a significant location. Meghalaya's tertiary coalfields are located in the Jaintia Hills, Khasi Hills, and Garo Hills.

questions.question: Which of the following is also known as Gelena?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is also known as Gelena?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e Lead sulphide.
  • What is Galena?
    • Galena is a lead sulfide mineral with a chemical composition of PbS.
    • It is the world's primary ore of lead and is mined from a large number of deposits in many countries.
    • It is found in igneous and metamorphic rocks in medium- to low-temperature hydrothermal veins.
    • In sedimentary rocks it occurs as veins, breccia cements, isolated grains, and as replacements of limestone and dolostone.
    • Galena is very easy to identify. Freshly broken pieces exhibit perfect cleavage in three directions that intersect at 90 degrees.
    • It has a distinct silver color and a bright metallic luster. Galena tarnishes to a dull gray.
    • Because lead is a primary element in galena, the mineral has a high specific gravity (7.4 to 7.6) that is immediately noticed when picking up even small pieces.
    • Galena is soft with a Mohs hardness of 2.5+ and produces a gray to black streak.
    • Crystals are common and they usually are cubes, octahedrons, or modifications.

questions.question: According to Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Government of India (2021-2022), which state in India is the largest producer of natural gas?
questions.questionHtml: According to Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Government of India (2021-2022), which state in India is the largest producer of natural gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Assam.

Key Points

  • Assam:-
    • According to the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Government of India (2021-2022), Assam is the largest producer of natural gas in India. Here are some bullet points to explain the answer:
    • Assam accounts for about 53% of India's total natural gas production.
    • The state has several natural gas fields, including the Digboi, Naharkatiya, and Rudrasagar fields.
    • The production of natural gas in Assam has been increasing steadily over the years. In 2019-20, the state produced over 5,000 million cubic meters of natural gas.
    • The natural gas produced in Assam is used for various purposes, including power generation, industrial use, and domestic use. 

Additional Information

  • Andhra Pradesh:-
    • Andhra Pradesh is not a significant producer of natural gas.
    • The state has some natural gas reserves, but they are not yet fully developed. 
  • Maharashtra:
    • Maharashtra is the second-largest producer of natural gas in India.
    • The state has several natural gas fields, including the Mumbai High field, which is one of the largest offshore fields in the world.
  • Tamil Nadu:
    • Tamil Nadu is not a significant producer of natural gas.
    • The state has some natural gas reserves, but they are not yet fully developed.

questions.question: Which of the following minerals is NOT found in rivers (alluvial placers) and on the coast, especially beaches (beach placers)?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following minerals is NOT found in rivers (alluvial placers) and on the coast, especially beaches (beach placers)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bauxite.

Key Points

  • The main minerals and metals associated with placer deposits are gold, cassiterite (tin), platinum, diamonds, magnetite, and some gemstones.
  • The two most important kinds of placers are stream (alluvial) and beach placers.
    • Hence Bauxite is the correct answer.
  • Beach placers are formed in sand and gravel deposited along the edge of large bodies of water and are typically found where streams or rivers flow into a large body of water.
  • Materials gather as beach placers by continuous wave action and currents.

Additional Information

  • Bauxite is a sedimentary rock with a relatively high aluminium content.
  • It is the world's main source of aluminium and gallium.
  • Bauxite is a naturally happen, heterogeneous material composed primarily of one or more aluminium hydroxide minerals, plus various mixtures of silica, iron oxide, titania, aluminosilicate, and other impurities in minor or trace amounts.
  • The main uses of bauxite are multipurpose covering metallurgy, chemical industries, as raw material in building and road aggregates.

questions.question: Which mineral composed of silicon and oxygen with chemical composition of SiO 2 is mainly used in glass making, abrasive, foundry sand, hydraulic fracturing proppant, gemstone?
questions.questionHtml: Which mineral composed of silicon and oxygen with chemical composition of SiO<sub>2</sub> is mainly used in glass making, abrasive, foundry sand, hydraulic fracturing proppant, gemstone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is QuartzKey Points

  • The mineral that is composed of silicon and oxygen with the chemical composition of SiO₂ and is mainly used in glass making, abrasive, foundry sand, hydraulic fracturing proppant, and gemstone is Quartz
  • Quartz is a primary raw material used in the production of glass, including container glass, flat glass, and specialty glass (like optical and fiber optics).
  • Due to its hardness, quartz is used as an abrasive material in sandpaper, grinding wheels, and other polishing applications.
  •  Quartz is utilized in foundry sands because of its high melting point and resistance to thermal shock, making it ideal for creating molds for metal casting.

Additional Information

  • Olivine
    • A silicate mineral that's usually green in color and is made up of iron, magnesium, and silica.
    • It's often found in igneous rocks that are mafic or ultramafic.
    • Olivine is not as stable as quartz and can break down into clay minerals during weathering. 
  • Muscovite
    • A mica that's a good conductor of heat but not electricity.
    • The Kodarma area in Jharkhand, India is famous for its muscovite mines, which produce the largest quantity of muscovite in the world. 
  • Augite
    • A mineral that's rich in iron and/or magnesium, and is typically black or dark green in color.

questions.question: What is the most stable mineral during the process of weathering?
questions.questionHtml: What is the most stable mineral during the process of weathering?
questions.solution: Quartz is the most stable mineral during the process of weathering because it is highly resistant to chemical and physical weathering. Quartz is a mineral composed of silicon and oxygen atoms in a continuous framework of SiO4 siliconoxygen tetrahedra.

questions.question: The premier iron ore exporting port of India is situated in ______.
questions.questionHtml: The premier iron ore exporting port of India is situated in ______.
questions.solution: The premier iron ore exporting port of India is situated in Goa. Marmagao port in Goa is the main port used by the nation to export iron ore. Almost 50% of India's exports of iron ore come from this port. It is located on India's west coast.

questions.question: Which of the following sedimentary minerals, known to everyone as 'salt', usually form in arid climates where seawater evaporates?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following sedimentary minerals, known to everyone as 'salt', usually form in arid climates where seawater evaporates?
questions.solution: Halite is a sedimentary mineral that forms in arid climates where sea water evaporates, leaving behind salt deposits. Halite is also known as rock salt and is commonly used as a seasoning or preservative in food.

questions.question: The HPCL Rajasthan Refinery Ltd (HRRL) is being constructed in which district (as of December 2022)?
questions.questionHtml: The HPCL Rajasthan Refinery Ltd (HRRL) is being constructed in which district (as of December 2022)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is BarmerKey Points

  •  The HPCL Rajasthan Refinery Ltd (HRRL) is being constructed in the Balotra district of Rajasthan, in the Pachpadra Tehsil: 
  • The HRRR is a joint venture between the Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) and the Government of Rajasthan (GoR): 
  • HPCL holds 74% of the stake in the HRRR, while the GoR holds the remaining 26%. 
  • The HRRR is a 9 Million Metric Tonnes Per Annum (MMTPA) refinery and petrochemical complex.
  • It can process a mix of imported and local crudes. 
  • Expansion
  • The refinery capacity is planned to be expanded from 9.0 to 18.0 MMTPA in the future. 
  • Environmental benefits
  • The refinery complex includes a wetland habitat for migratory birds, natural surface water body rejuvenation, and avenue plantation. 
  • Completion
  • The project was originally scheduled for completion by December 2022, but was delayed due to pandemic-related shutdowns.
  • The refinery is now expected to be commissioned by January 2025.
